name: upwork-mcp
description: Upwork (deals): me, search_postings, get_posting, bid_status, list_messages, send_message. Every too

platform_mcp_upwork_client_id.title: PLATFORM_MCP_UPWORK_CLIENT_ID
platform_mcp_upwork_client_id.description: Client ID of an approved Upwork API key (apply at https://www.upwork.com/developer/keys/apply; Upwork reviews every key).

platform_mcp_upwork_client_secret.title: PLATFORM_MCP_UPWORK_CLIENT_SECRET
platform_mcp_upwork_client_secret.description: Client secret of the same API key (form body of the refresh_token grant).

platform_mcp_upwork_refresh_token.title: PLATFORM_MCP_UPWORK_REFRESH_TOKEN
platform_mcp_upwork_refresh_token.description: Refresh token from the Authorization Code Grant for the freelancer/agency account; the runtime mints access tokens (TTL 86400 s) at https://www.upwork.com/api/v3/oauth2/token and keeps the rotated refresh_token each response returns (set PLATFORM_MCP_STATE_DIR to persist it).

platform_mcp_upwork_tenant_id.title: PLATFORM_MCP_UPWORK_TENANT_ID
platform_mcp_upwork_tenant_id.description: Optional organization id sent as X-Upwork-API-TenantId (the execution context; without it the user's default organization is used).

tools.name: me
tools.description: POST /graphql query { user { id nid rid } } — the authenticated user (account.data.user).

tools.name: search_postings
tools.description: POST https://api.upwork.com/graphql marketplaceJobPostingsSearch (permission 'Read marketplace Job Postings'), searchType USER_JOBS_SEARCH, newest first (sortAttributes RECENCY), following the documented real-life example. `query` → searchExpression_eq (partial Lucene syntax); `category` → categoryIds_any[0] (an Upwork category id); `min_budget` → budgetRange_eq.rangeStart (whole number; hourly jobs are returned regardless of budget); page/limit → pagination_eq {after: offset as a string, as in the example's "0", first: limit}. Money values are strings (amount.rawValue / displayValue, hourlyBudgetMin/Max) and skills are {name} objects, so they stay in raw; the job page is https://www.upwork.com/jobs/~<raw.node.ciphertext>. GraphQL failures arrive as HTTP 200 with errors[]: a null data is reported as an error, but a permission error on the field alone yields an empty list.

tools.name: get_posting
tools.description: POST /graphql marketplaceJobPosting(id) with the documented fields (content.title/description, contractTerms.contractType, clientCompanyPublic.id in raw). id is the job posting id (the search result id).

tools.name: bid_status
tools.description: POST /graphql vendorProposal(id) → status.status (VendorProposalStatusName: Accepted, Declined, Withdrawn, Offered, Activated, Archived, Hired, Pending); viewedByClient in raw. For freelancers/agencies (permission 'Client Proposals - Read And Write Access'); the agency context follows X-Upwork-API-TenantId.

tools.name: list_messages
tools.description: POST /graphql roomStories(filter: {roomId_eq, storyFilter.pagination {after: "", first}}) as in the documented example. thread_id is the room id (e.g. room_d4ad…) and is required by the API. Only the first `limit` stories are returned (cursor paging is not followed; page is ignored).

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: POST /graphql createRoomStoryV2(input: {roomId, message}) — posts a message into the Upwork room as the authenticated user (visible to the other party immediately).
